verses.translation: Then{H227} the sages{H2450} and the Pharisees{H6567} came{H935} to Yeshua{H3442} and said{H559} to him:

verses.translation: Why{H4100} do your disciples{H8527} transgress{H5674} the enactments of the ancients{H7223}, for they do not wash{H7364} their hands{H3027} before{H6924} eating{H398}?

one_way_hebrew: תקנות — TAKKANOT: the rabbis' own legal category for post-biblical enactments. The Hebrew text names the handwashing rule for exactly what Jewish law calls it — a takkanah, a human enactment, not a Torah command — so the whole dispute is framed as Torah versus takkanah from its first word. Greek παράδοσις ('tradition') blurs the legal category; the Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew likewise reads 'the Tiqunim of the ancient ones.'
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (15:2): תלמידך] תלמידיך ABDEFH; הראשונות] הראשונית AH.

verses.translation: And Yeshua{H3442} said{H559} to them: And why{H4100} do you transgress{H5674} the sayings{H3982} of El{H410} for the sake of{H1157} your enactments?

one_way_hebrew: מאמרי האל — 'the SAYINGS of El' (מאמר, Esther's word, Esth 1:15; 2:20 — and the ma'amarot by which the world was made in rabbinic idiom): God's spoken decrees set against your takkanot. The rejoinder is a perfect halakhic counter-thrust — you plead an enactment; you are voiding a decree.

verses.translation: For El{H410} said{H559}: Honor{H3513} your father{H1} and your mother{H517}; and, He who smites{H5221} his father or his mother shall surely be put to death{H4191}.

one_way_hebrew: Two Torah texts quoted letter-perfect: כבד את אביך ואת אמך (Exod 20:12) and ומכה אביו ואמו מות יומת (Exod 21:15 — the SMITER). Greek Matthew's second citation is Exod 21:17, the CURSER (ὁ κακολογῶν); the Hebrew text cites the neighboring statute verbatim instead — a Hebrew author quoting the Torah scroll he knows, not back-translating the Greek's choice. The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew has the curser, with the Greek.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (15:4): אמר] יאמר EF.

verses.translation: But you say{H559} that whatever word{H1697} a man{H120} says{H559} to his father{H1} and to his mother{H517} — that by whatever freewill offering{H5071} he gives{H5414}, for that sin{H2399} it will be atoned{H3722} for him, that iniquity{H5771}.

one_way_hebrew: The korban-vow is stated in the Torah's own sacrificial vocabulary: נדבה (H5071, the freewill offering of Lev 22:18-23), כפר (H3722, atonement), עון (H5771, iniquity). Greek Matthew has only δῶρον ('a gift'); the Hebrew exposes the system being condemned — a donation offered as atonement while the commandment to honor parents goes unkept. Sacrifice pleaded against obedience is the exact case of Hos 6:6, already quoted at 12:7.
translation_notes: The syntax is compressed; Howard renders: 'whatever word a man should say to his father and mother in regard to any donation he might give for him as a sinner, this iniquity itself will be made void to him.'

verses.translation: And so he does not honor{H3513} his father{H1} and his mother{H517} — and you despise{H959} the sayings{H561} of El{H410} by your enactments.

O priests that despise (בוזי) my name'). The Hebrew closes the argument on Malachi's hinge-pair; Greek ἠκυρώσατε ('ye made void') is legal, not prophetic.

verses.translation: Thus{H3541} says{H559} YHWH{H3068}: Because{H3282} this{H2088} people{H5971} draws near{H5066} with its mouth{H6310}, and with its lips{H8193} they honor me{H3513}, but its heart{H3820} is far{H7368} from me,

one_way_hebrew: Isa 29:13 in the Masoretic text's own consonants — יען כי נגש העם הזה בפיו ובשפתיו כבדוני ולבו רחק ממני — prefaced with the prophetic messenger-formula כה אמר ה׳ ('Thus says YHWH'): the Hebrew author introduces Scripture the way Scripture introduces itself. Greek Matthew quotes the LXX's divergent form; the Shem Tov text carries the MT.

verses.translation: and their fear{H3374} of me is a commandment{H4687} of men{H582}, learned by rote{H3925}.

one_way_hebrew: Isa 29:13b VERBATIM from the MT: ותהי יראתם אתי מצות אנשים מלמדה — 'their fear of me is a commandment of men learned by rote.' Greek Matthew (following the LXX) reads 'in vain do they worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men' — a different sentence. No back-translator from that Greek arrives at the Masoretic clause letter-perfect; the Hebrew text is quoting the Hebrew Bible directly. And the MT's own words are the sharper indictment of the takkanot-dispute: a man-taught commandment has replaced the fear of YHWH.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (15:9): יראתם...מלומדה] omit G.

verses.translation: That which enters through{H1157} the mouth{H6310} does not soil the man{H120}, but{H61} that which goes out{H3318} of the mouth soils the man.

greek_deviations: The verb is לכלך — everyday rabbinic Hebrew for 'to DIRTY, soil' (Howard: 'does not soil the man') — not טמא, the Torah's term for ritual defilement. The Hebrew saying never enters the vocabulary of Lev 11 at all: it stays in the register of the handwashing takkanah it answers (v. 2), and its conclusion is drawn at v. 20 in the same word. Greek κοινοῖ ('makes common/defiles') imports the purity category the Hebrew deliberately avoids — and on the Greek word a whole doctrine of abolished food-laws was built. In the Hebrew there is nothing to abolish: unwashed hands do not dirty a man; the Torah is not in question.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (15:11): היוצא] מה שיוצא A; בעד הפה] בפה האדם H.

verses.translation: Then{H227} his disciples{H8527} drew near{H7126} to him and said{H559} to him: Know{H3045} that the Pharisees{H6567} are perplexed{H943} because of this{H2088} word{H1697}.

one_way_hebrew: נבוכים (H943) — the perplexity-word once more (11:6; 13:21; 13:57): in this text the offended are always the ENTANGLED (Exod 14:3), those who cannot find their way through; Greek ἐσκανδαλίσθησαν flattens the chain.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (15:12): ויאמרו] ואמרו A.

verses.translation: And Yeshua{H3442} answered{H6030} them: Every planting{H5194} which my Father{H1} who is in the heavens{H8064} did not plant{H5193} will be destroyed{H7843}.

one_way_hebrew: נטע — the planting verb of Israel's election (Exod 15:17, 'thou shalt plant them in the mountain of thine inheritance'; Isa 60:21, 'the branch of my planting'; Jer 45:4, 'that which I have planted I will pluck up'). The takkanot are a planting the Father did not plant; תשחת (H7843) is the flood-narrative's destruction verb (Gen 6:13, cf. 24:39).

verses.translation: Leave{H3240} them — for the blind{H5787} are leading{H1869} the blind; and if a blind man leads another{H312} blind man, both{H8147} will fall{H5307} into a pit{H953}.

one_way_hebrew: מדריכים (H1869, darak) — 'cause to tread, lead in the way': Isaiah's guidance verb (Isa 42:16, 'I will bring the blind by a way they knew not... I will lead them'); the false guides do for harm what YHWH there does for mercy. בור (H953) — the cistern-pit of Gen 37:24 and Jer 38:6.

verses.translation: And Petros answered{H6030} him: My master{H113}, explain{H6567} to us this{H2063} riddle{H2420}.

In two words the request speaks the Hebrew Bible's own hermeneutical vocabulary; Greek 'declare unto us this parable' has neither term.

one_way_hebrew: מבלי דעת — 'without DA'AT': the Hosea-phrase (Hos 4:6, 'my people are destroyed מבלי הדעת, for lack of knowledge'; Isa 5:13) — the rebuke to the disciples borrows the prophets' indictment of Israel.

verses.translation: Do you not understand{H995} that everything which enters through{H1157} the mouth{H6310} goes{H1980} to the belly{H990}, and all of it goes out through the natural place{H4725}?

translation_notes: המקום הטבעי — 'the NATURAL place': the euphemism of medieval Hebrew science (teva, 'nature,' is post-biblical; the phrase is at home in Spanish-Hebrew philosophical prose). Greek ἀφεδρών ('latrine') is blunter. A fourteenth-century Hebrew text speaks its own century's Hebrew here, exactly as a living text does.

verses.translation: But that which goes out{H3318} through{H1157} the mouth{H6310} is stirred{H5128} from the heart{H3820}, and this is what soils the man{H120}.
Because from the profaned{H2490} heart{H3820} go out{H3318} deceit{H8649}, and murder{H7523}, and adulteries{H5004}, and thefts{H1591}, and testimony{H5715} of lies{H8267}, and curses{H7045}.

one_way_hebrew: The catalogue walks the second table of the Ten Words in the Torah's own roots and order: רציחה (רצח, Exod 20:13), נאופים (נאף, 20:14), גנבות (גנב, 20:15), עדות שקרים (עד שקר, 20:16) — with תרמית (Jer 14:14's word for lying prophecy) at the head and קללות at the tail. The evil heart is indicted by the Decalogue itself; Greek Matthew's list (φόνοι, μοιχεῖαι, πορνεῖαι, κλοπαί...) translates the substance and loses the commandments' own consonants.
שמחלל הלב — 'the PROFANED heart' (חלל, H2490, the profaning verb of 12:5): Howard renders 'the defiled heart.' What defiles is not food but a heart profaned.
translation_notes: והרציחה is written twice in the base ms (a dittograph); translated once.
textual_notes: The scan reads שקרים; the circulating transcription's שפרים is a typo, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (15:19): ועדות] ועדיות A.

verses.translation: And all these{H428} things{H1697} are what confound the man{H120}; indeed{H551}, eating{H398} without{H1097} the washing{H7364} of hands{H3027} does not soil the man.

greek_deviations: The discourse closes exactly where it opened (v. 2): on the handwashing takkanah — 'eating without the washing of hands does not SOIL (מלכלכת) the man.' Nothing about clean and unclean foods enters the sentence in Hebrew; the verdict voids an enactment of men (vv. 2, 9) and leaves the Torah's food-laws untouched. The symbol deepens the command — the profaned heart is the real uncleanness — it does not dissolve a single statute.
textual_notes: The scan reads מלכלכת; the circulating transcription's מלכלכלת is a typo, corrected here.

verses.translation: And they all ate{H398} and were satisfied{H7646}, and there was left over{H3498} seven{H7651} seahs{H5429}.

one_way_hebrew: והותר (H3498, yathar) — the exact hiphil of Elisha's bread-multiplication: 'They shall eat, and shall leave thereof (ואכול והותר)... and they did eat, and left thereof (ויותרו)' (2 Kgs 4:43-44). The feeding of the four thousand closes on the prophet-miracle's own verb — eat, be satisfied, and leave over — plus the seah-measure of Gen 18:6 (cf. 13:33; 14:20). Greek 'they took up of the broken pieces seven baskets' loses Elisha entirely.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (15:37): ויאכלו] ואכלו DEFG; וישבעו] ושבעו ACDEFG; והותר] ומהנשאר מלאו ABDEF ('and from what remained they filled'), והושאר מלאו G — Howard renders '(from that which was remaining they filled) seven seahs.'

translation_notes: מאצידונייא — 'Macedonia' (so Howard's English): a garbled place-name where Greek Matthew reads Magadan/Magdala. The mss splinter (מאסידוניאה, מאצידוניא, מסאדוניא, מצדוניאה) — European copyists wrestling an unfamiliar Galilean name into a familiar one; Vat. Ebr. 100 reads 'the country of Magdala.' ספינה — Jonah's ship-word again (cf. 14:29).

chapter_notes.summary: Matthew 15 in the Shem Tov Hebrew is the Torah-versus-takkanah chapter, and the Hebrew keeps the legal categories straight where the Greek blurred them. (1) The dispute is named from the first word as about תקנות — TAKKANOT, the rabbis' own term for human enactments (15:2; 'your takkanot' vv. 3, 6; Vat. Ebr. 100 likewise 'Tiqunim') — against מאמרי האל, 'the sayings of El': Greek 'tradition' vs 'commandment' loses the halakhic precision. (2) The defilement-verb throughout is לכלך — 'to SOIL, dirty' (vv. 11, 18, 20) — everyday Hebrew, not טמא: the verdict 'eating without washing of hands does not soil the man' voids a handwashing enactment and never touches Lev 11; the Greek's κοινόω imported the ritual category on which food-law abolition was later built. (3) 15:8-9 quote Isa 29:13 from the MASORETIC TEXT verbatim — including 'their fear of me is a commandment of men learned by rote' — where Greek Matthew follows the divergent LXX ('in vain do they worship me...'); the citation opens with the messenger-formula כה אמר ה״, the Name written with the reverent abbreviation. (4) 15:4 cites Exod 21:15 (the SMITER of father and mother) where Greek cites 21:17 (the curser); 15:5 states the korban-vow in the Torah's own sacrificial terms (נדבה, כפר, עון); 15:6 closes on Mal 1:6's honor/despise pair. (5) 15:19's catalogue of the heart walks the Decalogue's second table in the commandments' own roots and order (רצח, נאף, גנב, עד שקר). (6) 15:21 pairs Tyre with SODOM again (cf. 11:21-24; mss assimilate to Sidon); the Canaanite woman comes 'from the lands of the east' (not in Greek), cries the Psalter's חנני and עזרני, and answers the loaf (פת) with the fragments (פתיתים) — a one-root word-play invisible in Greek; 15:24's 'lost sheep' is Jer 50:6's exact phrase (ms A substitutes Ezek 34:16's 'driven away'). (7) 15:30-31 gather Zeph 3:19's LIMPING ones and enact Isa 35:5-6 with the mute speaking; 15:37 closes the feeding with Elisha's own miracle-verb והותר (2 Kgs 4:43-44) and the seah-measure; 15:38 counts by the Exodus census-formula. (8) 15:32 reads 'TWO days' (Greek: three); 15:39 lands at 'Macedonia' — a garbled Magadan the mss splinter over (Vat. Ebr. 100: Magdala). Rabbinic-Hebrew fingerprints throughout: רחמנות, תענית, ע״ג, המקום הטבעי, נבוכים again at 15:12. Shem Tov's section divisions fall at vv. 1 (Perek 67), 21 (68), 29 (69), and 39 (70).
